clusters.rationale: One canonical base-ten place model derives digit positions, powers of ten, decimal shifts, aligned comparison, rounding, and equivalent scaling of a decimal divisor. Distinct tasks remain explicit modes; no task is reduced to recognition-only MCQ.
Exact but smaller. Decimal division is subsumed truthfully by the larger base-ten closure; remainder interpretation and long division remain separate quotient-construction work.
Shares linear equations but mixes line reading, comparison, back-substitution, and solving systems. A single surface would either leak solutions or collapse construction into recognition.
All can draw on a number line, but rounding intervals, inequality sets, root classification, and density are different mathematical truth models.
Arbitrary-base exponent evaluation does not share the decimal digit-position invariant. Excluding it yields the larger exact base-ten family selected above.
